Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

## PR Description

Closes #1763
# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity.
- Full default suite: `+11961 ~62`, **zero failures attributable to this change** — `dart analyze` clean, CRAP diff gate OK, `test/providers/` green in isolation.

### Notes
- All 17 suite failures attributed by controlled experiment: `test/browser_ext/` ×5 fail identically on the pre-fix tree (no DBus for Chrome; owns `browser-ext.yml`); 11 integration legs fail only when the dev agent's `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` env leaks into spawned sessions — **green with the `FA*` vars scrubbed**, incl. the new SIGTERM assertion; `composer_tui_grid_pty` ×1 is a pre-existing render flake (3/3 failures pre-fix).

+library;

+import 'dart:io';
+
+/// The env var carrying the protected pid set into every bash tool call
+/// (space-separated): the harness pid, its ancestor chain up to init, and
+/// the harness process group. The `kill()` prelude and both shims read it.
+const String bashGuardPidsEnv = 'FA_PROTECTED_PIDS';
+
+/// The env var carrying the shim dir path into every bash tool call (the
+/// PATH itself is prepended by `_environment`; the variable exists so the
+/// contract has one owner here).
+const String bashGuardShimDirEnv = 'FA_GUARD_SHIM_DIR';
+
+/// The guard prelude prepended to every bash tool script (POSIX):
+///
+/// - `set --` restores `sh -c` positional-parameter parity (`$#` = 0, empty
+///   `"$@"`) — the `. "$1"` delivery otherwise leaves the script path as
+///   `$1`.
+/// - `kill()` filters [bashGuardPidsEnv] pids (and their `-pgid` group
+///   targets) out of the arguments before invoking the real `kill`. No
+///   protected hit → the call is passed through byte-identical. Every
+///   construct is `set -e`/`set -u`-safe (if-chains, guarded expansions).
+String bashGuardPrelude() =>
+    '''
+# ── fa bash-guard (gh-1763): self-defense prelude ──────────────────────
+# Restore sh -c positional-parameter parity, then keep kill() from
+# signaling the harness/ancestor pids exported via $bashGuardPidsEnv.
+set --
+kill() {
+  __fa_rest=''
+  __fa_pids_left=0
+  __fa_hit=0
+  for __fa_a in "\$@"; do
+    case "\$__fa_a" in
+      ''|-|--|%*|-[A-Za-z]*)
+        __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+        ;;
+      -[0-9]*)
+        __fa_n="\${__fa_a#-}"
+        __fa_keep=1
+        for __fa_p in \${$bashGuardPidsEnv:-}; do
+          if [ "\$__fa_n" = "\$__fa_p" ]; then __fa_keep=0; break; fi
+        done
+        if [ "\$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
+          __fa_hit=1
+        else
+          __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+        fi
+        ;;
+      *)
+        __fa_keep=1
+        for __fa_p in \${$bashGuardPidsEnv:-}; do
+          if [ "\$__fa_a" = "\$__fa_p" ]; then __fa_keep=0; break; fi
+        done
+        if [ "\$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
+          __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+          __fa_pids_left=\$((__fa_pids_left + 1))
+        else
+          __fa_hit=1
+        fi
+        ;;
+    esac
+  done
+  if [ "\$__fa_hit" = 0 ]; then
+    command kill "\$@"
+    return
+  fi
+  __fa_rc=0
+  if [ "\$__fa_pids_left" -gt 0 ]; then
+    # shellcheck disable=SC2086 — every surviving arg is a single word.
+    command kill \$__fa_rest || __fa_rc=\$?
+  fi
+  echo 'fa: kill skipped protected pid(s) (gh-1763 bash-guard)' >&2
+  return "\$__fa_rc"
+}
+''';
+
+/// The `pkill` PATH shim: expands the match with the REAL `pgrep` (the
+/// same selection engine and flags), filters the protected pids, the
+/// invoking shell (`PPID`) and the shim itself, then signals the rest with
+/// the requested signal (default `SIGTERM`). Selection shapes the shim
+/// does not model (signal after the pattern, `-u root`, `-t tty`, `-n`,
+/// `-o`, …) exec the real `pkill` — honest behavior over silent guessing.
+String buildPkillShim({required String realPkill, required String realPgrep}) =>
+    r'''#!/bin/sh
+# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
+# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
+set -u
+FA_REAL_PKILL='__FA_REAL_PKILL__'
+FA_REAL_PGREP='__FA_REAL_PGREP__'
+
+sig=''
+sel=''
+# Flags that would corrupt the victim set if they reached pgrep (c = count
+# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)
+# never enter the guarded path — the real pkill decides.
+for a in "$@"; do
+  case "$a" in
+    -[a-zA-Z]*)
+      fa_body="${a#-}"
+      case "$fa_body" in
+        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;
+      esac
+      fa_rest="$fa_body"
+      while [ -n "$fa_rest" ]; do
+        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
+        case "$fa_c" in
+          [cv]) exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@" ;;
+        esac
+        fa_rest="${fa_rest#?}"
+      done
+      ;;
+  esac

+    --signal) sig="${2-}"; shift 2 ;;
+    --signal=*) sig="${1#--signal=}"; shift ;;
+    --) shift; break ;;
+    -[0-9]*) sig="$1"; shift ;;
+    -[Ss][Ii][Gg][A-Za-z]*|-[A-Z][A-Z]*) sig="$1"; shift ;;
+    -*) sel="$sel $1"; shift ;;
+    *) break ;;
+  esac

+# flags interleaved with it, extra operands — is the real pkill's call.

+rc=$?

## PR Description

Closes #1763
# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity.
- Full default suite: `+11961 ~62`, **zero failures attributable to this change** — `dart analyze` clean, CRAP diff gate OK, `test/providers/` green in isolation.

### Notes
- All 17 suite failures attributed by controlled experiment: `test/browser_ext/` ×5 fail identically on the pre-fix tree (no DBus for Chrome; owns `browser-ext.yml`); 11 integration legs fail only when the dev agent's `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` env leaks into spawned sessions — **green with the `FA*` vars scrubbed**, incl. the new SIGTERM assertion; `composer_tui_grid_pty` ×1 is a pre-existing render flake (3/3 failures pre-fix).

+/// the harness process group. The `kill()` prelude and both shims read it.
+const String bashGuardPidsEnv = 'FA_PROTECTED_PIDS';
+
+/// The env var carrying the shim dir path into every bash tool call (the
+/// PATH itself is prepended by `_environment`; the variable exists so the
+/// contract has one owner here).
+const String bashGuardShimDirEnv = 'FA_GUARD_SHIM_DIR';
+
+/// The guard prelude prepended to every bash tool script (POSIX):
+///
+/// - `set --` restores `sh -c` positional-parameter parity (`$#` = 0, empty
+///   `"$@"`) — the `. "$1"` delivery otherwise leaves the script path as
+///   `$1`.
+/// - `kill()` filters [bashGuardPidsEnv] pids (and their `-pgid` group
+///   targets) out of the arguments before invoking the real `kill`. No
+///   protected hit → the call is passed through byte-identical. Every
+///   construct is `set -e`/`set -u`-safe (if-chains, guarded expansions).
+String bashGuardPrelude() =>
+    '''
+# ── fa bash-guard (gh-1763): self-defense prelude ──────────────────────
+# Restore sh -c positional-parameter parity, then keep kill() from
+# signaling the harness/ancestor pids exported via $bashGuardPidsEnv.
+set --
+kill() {
+  __fa_rest=''
+  __fa_pids_left=0
+  __fa_hit=0
+  for __fa_a in "\$@"; do
+    case "\$__fa_a" in
+      ''|-|--|%*|-[A-Za-z]*)
+        __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+        ;;
+      -[0-9]*)
+        __fa_n="\${__fa_a#-}"
+        __fa_keep=1
+        for __fa_p in \${$bashGuardPidsEnv:-}; do
+          if [ "\$__fa_n" = "\$__fa_p" ]; then __fa_keep=0; break; fi
+        done
+        if [ "\$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
+          __fa_hit=1
+        else
+          __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+        fi
+        ;;
+      *)
+        __fa_keep=1
+        for __fa_p in \${$bashGuardPidsEnv:-}; do
+          if [ "\$__fa_a" = "\$__fa_p" ]; then __fa_keep=0; break; fi
+        done
+        if [ "\$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
+          __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+          __fa_pids_left=\$((__fa_pids_left + 1))
+        else
+          __fa_hit=1
+        fi
+        ;;
+    esac
+  done
+  if [ "\$__fa_hit" = 0 ]; then
+    command kill "\$@"
+    return
+  fi
+  __fa_rc=0

+  fi

+String buildPkillShim({required String realPkill, required String realPgrep}) =>
+    r'''#!/bin/sh

+# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.

+FA_REAL_PKILL='__FA_REAL_PKILL__'
+FA_REAL_PGREP='__FA_REAL_PGREP__'

+sig=''
+sel=''

+      esac
+      fa_rest="$fa_body"

+        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
+        case "$fa_c" in
+          [cv]) exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@" ;;
+        esac
+        fa_rest="${fa_rest#?}"
+      done

+    --signal=*) sig="${1#--signal=}"; shift ;;

+    -[Ss][Ii][Gg][A-Za-z]*|-[A-Z][A-Z]*) sig="$1"; shift ;;

+  else
+    kill -TERM "$p" 2>/dev/null && out=1
+  fi
+done

In procps-ng, pkill and pgrep share a binary (pkill is pgrep with different behavior); `pkill -l`... The help output above doesn't show -l for pkill. ## PR Description

Closes #1763
# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity.
- Full default suite: `+11961 ~62`, **zero failures attributable to this change** — `dart analyze` clean, CRAP diff gate OK, `test/providers/` green in isolation.

### Notes
- All 17 suite failures attributed by controlled experiment: `test/browser_ext/` ×5 fail identically on the pre-fix tree (no DBus for Chrome; owns `browser-ext.yml`); 11 integration legs fail only when the dev agent's `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` env leaks into spawned sessions — **green with the `FA*` vars scrubbed**, incl. the new SIGTERM assertion; `composer_tui_grid_pty` ×1 is a pre-existing render flake (3/3 failures pre-fix).

+/// PATH itself is prepended by `_environment`; the variable exists so the
+/// contract has one owner here).
+const String bashGuardShimDirEnv = 'FA_GUARD_SHIM_DIR';

+/// The guard prelude prepended to every bash tool script (POSIX):
+///
+/// - `set --` restores `sh -c` positional-parameter parity (`$#` = 0, empty

+# ── fa bash-guard (gh-1763): self-defense prelude ──────────────────────
+# Restore sh -c positional-parameter parity, then keep kill() from
+# signaling the harness/ancestor pids exported via $bashGuardPidsEnv.
+set --
+kill() {
+  __fa_rest=''
+  __fa_pids_left=0
+  __fa_hit=0
+  for __fa_a in "\$@"; do
+    case "\$__fa_a" in
+      ''|-|--|%*|-[A-Za-z]*)
+        __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+        ;;
+      -[0-9]*)
+        __fa_n="\${__fa_a#-}"
+        __fa_keep=1
+        for __fa_p in \${$bashGuardPidsEnv:-}; do
+          if [ "\$__fa_n" = "\$__fa_p" ]; then __fa_keep=0; break; fi
+        done
+        if [ "\$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
+          __fa_hit=1
+        else
+          __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+        fi
+        ;;
+      *)
+        __fa_keep=1
+        for __fa_p in \${$bashGuardPidsEnv:-}; do
+          if [ "\$__fa_a" = "\$__fa_p" ]; then __fa_keep=0; break; fi
+        done
+        if [ "\$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
+          __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+          __fa_pids_left=\$((__fa_pids_left + 1))
+        else
+          __fa_hit=1
+        fi

+String buildPkillShim({required String realPkill, required String realPgrep}) =>
+    r'''#!/bin/sh

+# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.

+FA_REAL_PKILL='__FA_REAL_PKILL__'
+FA_REAL_PGREP='__FA_REAL_PGREP__'
+
+sig=''
+sel=''

+    -[a-zA-Z]*)
+      fa_body="${a#-}"

+      fa_rest="$fa_body"

+    --signal=*) sig="${1#--signal=}"; shift ;;

+    -[Ss][Ii][Gg][A-Za-z]*|-[A-Z][A-Z]*) sig="$1"; shift ;;

+  fi

- `pkill` HAS `-e, --echo` — "display what is killed"! Interesting — `-e` is a pkill flag that DISPLAYS what is killed while still signaling. In the shim: `-e` → first loop: char e → not c/v → rides in sel → pgrep -e? pgrep has no `-e`... pgrep options don't include -e. pgrep -e → invalid → rc=2 → fallback to real pkill. Fine.

In procps-ng, pkill and pgrep share a binary (pkill is pgrep with different behavior); `pkill -l`... The help output above doesn't show -l for pkill. Let me test `pkill -l` directly: `pkill -l fa_count_probe` — if it errors "invalid option", then the -l concern is moot (the shim: -l → sel → pgrep -l → prints pid+name → CUT → kill! - `pkill -e` (echo) — displays kills; pgrep lacks -e → fallback → honest. OK.

## PR Description

Closes #1763
# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity.
- Full default suite: `+11961 ~62`, **zero failures attributable to this change** — `dart analyze` clean, CRAP diff gate OK, `test/providers/` green in isolation.

### Notes
- All 17 suite failures attributed by controlled experiment: `test/browser_ext/` ×5 fail identically on the pre-fix tree (no DBus for Chrome; owns `browser-ext.yml`); 11 integration legs fail only when the dev agent's `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` env leaks into spawned sessions — **green with the `FA*` vars scrubbed**, incl. the new SIGTERM assertion; `composer_tui_grid_pty` ×1 is a pre-existing render flake (3/3 failures pre-fix).

+/// PATH itself is prepended by `_environment`; the variable exists so the
+/// contract has one owner here).
+const String bashGuardShimDirEnv = 'FA_GUARD_SHIM_DIR';

+/// The guard prelude prepended to every bash tool script (POSIX):
+///
+/// - `set --` restores `sh -c` positional-parameter parity (`$#` = 0, empty

+# ── fa bash-guard (gh-1763): self-defense prelude ──────────────────────
+# Restore sh -c positional-parameter parity, then keep kill() from
+# signaling the harness/ancestor pids exported via $bashGuardPidsEnv.
+set --
+kill() {
+  __fa_rest=''
+  __fa_pids_left=0
+  __fa_hit=0
+  for __fa_a in "\$@"; do
+    case "\$__fa_a" in
+      ''|-|--|%*|-[A-Za-z]*)
+        __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+        ;;
+      -[0-9]*)
+        __fa_n="\${__fa_a#-}"
+        __fa_keep=1
+        for __fa_p in \${$bashGuardPidsEnv:-}; do
+          if [ "\$__fa_n" = "\$__fa_p" ]; then __fa_keep=0; break; fi
+        done
+        if [ "\$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
+          __fa_hit=1
+        else
+          __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+        fi
+        ;;
+      *)
+        __fa_keep=1
+        for __fa_p in \${$bashGuardPidsEnv:-}; do
+          if [ "\$__fa_a" = "\$__fa_p" ]; then __fa_keep=0; break; fi
+        done
+        if [ "\$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
+          __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+          __fa_pids_left=\$((__fa_pids_left + 1))
+        else
+          __fa_hit=1
+        fi

+String buildPkillShim({required String realPkill, required String realPgrep}) =>
+    r'''#!/bin/sh

+# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.

+FA_REAL_PKILL='__FA_REAL_PKILL__'
+FA_REAL_PGREP='__FA_REAL_PGREP__'
+
+sig=''
+sel=''

+    -[a-zA-Z]*)
+      fa_body="${a#-}"

+      fa_rest="$fa_body"

+    --signal=*) sig="${1#--signal=}"; shift ;;

+    -[Ss][Ii][Gg][A-Za-z]*|-[A-Z][A-Z]*) sig="$1"; shift ;;

+  fi

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1777
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1777
- **Title**: gh-1763 [BUG] bash tool pkill -f self-matches its own sh -c wrapper (exit -15) and aborts the fa session with exit 130 (gh-1746 run 39661276610)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1763` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +809
- **Deletions**: -32
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T22:14:35Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T00:21:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #1763
# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity.
- Full default suite: `+11961 ~62`, **zero failures attributable to this change** — `dart analyze` clean, CRAP diff gate OK, `test/providers/` green in isolation.

### Notes
- All 17 suite failures attributed by controlled experiment: `test/browser_ext/` ×5 fail identically on the pre-fix tree (no DBus for Chrome; owns `browser-ext.yml`); 11 integration legs fail only when the dev agent's `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` env leaks into spawned sessions — **green with the `FA*` vars scrubbed**, incl. the new SIGTERM assertion; `composer_tui_grid_pty` ×1 is a pre-existing render flake (3/3 failures pre-fix).

+library;
+
+import 'dart:io';
+
+/// The env var carrying the protected pid set into every bash tool call
+/// (space-separated): the harness pid, its ancestor chain up to init, and
+/// the harness process group. The `kill()` prelude and both shims read it.
+const String bashGuardPidsEnv = 'FA_PROTECTED_PIDS';
+
+/// The env var carrying the shim dir path into every bash tool call (the
+/// PATH itself is prepended by `_environment`; the variable exists so the
+/// contract has one owner here).
+const String bashGuardShimDirEnv = 'FA_GUARD_SHIM_DIR';
+
+/// The guard prelude prepended to every bash tool script (POSIX):
+///
+/// - `set --` restores `sh -c` positional-parameter parity (`$#` = 0, empty
+///   `"$@"`) — the `. "$1"` delivery otherwise leaves the script path as
+///   `$1`.
+/// - `kill()` filters [bashGuardPidsEnv] pids (and their `-pgid` group
+///   targets) out of the arguments before invoking the real `kill`. No
+///   protected hit → the call is passed through byte-identical. Every
+///   construct is `set -e`/`set -u`-safe (if-chains, guarded expansions).
+String bashGuardPrelude() =>
+    '''
+# ── fa bash-guard (gh-1763): self-defense prelude ──────────────────────
+# Restore sh -c positional-parameter parity, then keep kill() from
+# signaling the harness/ancestor pids exported via $bashGuardPidsEnv.
+set --
+kill() {
+  __fa_rest=''
+  __fa_pids_left=0
+  __fa_hit=0
+  for __fa_a in "\$@"; do
+    case "\$__fa_a" in
+      ''|-|--|%*|-[A-Za-z]*)
+        __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+        ;;
+      -[0-9]*)
+        __fa_n="\${__fa_a#-}"
+        __fa_keep=1
+        for __fa_p in \${$bashGuardPidsEnv:-}; do
+          if [ "\$__fa_n" = "\$__fa_p" ]; then __fa_keep=0; break; fi
+        done
+        if [ "\$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
+          __fa_hit=1
+        else
+          __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+        fi
+        ;;
+      *)
+        __fa_keep=1
+        for __fa_p in \${$bashGuardPidsEnv:-}; do
+          if [ "\$__fa_a" = "\$__fa_p" ]; then __fa_keep=0; break; fi
+        done
+        if [ "\$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
+          __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+          __fa_pids_left=\$((__fa_pids_left + 1))
+        else
+          __fa_hit=1
+        fi
+        ;;
+    esac
+  done
+  if [ "\$__fa_hit" = 0 ]; then
+    command kill "\$@"
+    return
+  fi
+  __fa_rc=0
+  if [ "\$__fa_pids_left" -gt 0 ]; then
+    # shellcheck disable=SC2086 — every surviving arg is a single word.
+    command kill \$__fa_rest || __fa_rc=\$?
+  fi
+  echo 'fa: kill skipped protected pid(s) (gh-1763 bash-guard)' >&2
+  return "\$__fa_rc"
+}
+''';
+
+/// The `pkill` PATH shim: expands the match with the REAL `pgrep` (the
+/// same selection engine and flags), filters the protected pids, the
+/// invoking shell (`PPID`) and the shim itself, then signals the rest with
+/// the requested signal (default `SIGTERM`). Selection shapes the shim
+/// does not model (signal after the pattern, `-u root`, `-t tty`, `-n`,
+/// `-o`, …) exec the real `pkill` — honest behavior over silent guessing.
+String buildPkillShim({required String realPkill, required String realPgrep}) =>
+    r'''#!/bin/sh
+# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
+# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
+set -u
+FA_REAL_PKILL='__FA_REAL_PKILL__'
+FA_REAL_PGREP='__FA_REAL_PGREP__'
+
+sig=''
+sel=''
+# Flags that would corrupt the victim set if they reached pgrep (c = count
+# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)
+# never enter the guarded path — the real pkill decides.
+for a in "$@"; do
+  case "$a" in
+    -[a-zA-Z]*)
+      fa_body="${a#-}"
+      case "$fa_body" in
+        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;
+      esac
+      fa_rest="$fa_body"
+      while [ -n "$fa_rest" ]; do
+        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
+        case "$fa_c" in
+          [cv]) exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@" ;;
+        esac
+        fa_rest="${fa_rest#?}"
+      done
+      ;;
+  esac
+done
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --signal) sig="${2-}"; shift 2 ;;
+    --signal=*) sig="${1#--signal=}"; shift ;;
+    --) shift; break ;;
+    -[0-9]*) sig="$1"; shift ;;
+    -[Ss][Ii][Gg][A-Za-z]*|-[A-Z][A-Z]*) sig="$1"; shift ;;
+    -*) sel="$sel $1"; shift ;;
+    *) break ;;
+  esac
+done
+# Exactly one operand (the pattern) must remain; anything else — unknown
+# flags interleaved with it, extra operands — is the real pkill's call.
+if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
+  exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@"
+fi
+
+# The selection flags ride along: pgrep shares pkill's selection engine.
+pids=$("$FA_REAL_PGREP" $sel "$@" 2>/dev/null)
+rc=$?
+if [ "$rc" -ge 2 ]; then
+  # pgrep rejected the selection (a flag it does not share): the real
+  # pkill decides, semantics stay honest.
+  exec "$FA_REAL_PKILL" "$@"
+fi
+[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
+# pgrep -l rows are "pid name" — keep the pid column.
+pids=$(printf '%s\n' "$pids" | cut -d' ' -f1)
+
+self=$$
+parent="${PPID:-}"
+out=0
+for p in $pids; do
+  case " ${FA_PROTECTED_PIDS:-} " in *" $p "*) continue ;; esac
+  if [ "$p" = "$parent" ] || [ "$p" = "$self" ]; then continue; fi
+  if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
+    kill "$sig" "$p" 2>/dev/null && out=1
+  else
+    kill -TERM "$p" 2>/dev/null && out=1
+  fi
+done
+[ "$out" -eq 1 ] && exit 0
+exit 1
+'''
+        .replaceAll('__FA_REAL_PKILL__', realPkill)
+        .replaceAll('__FA_REAL_PGREP__', realPgrep);
+
+/// The `killall` PATH shim: exact comm-name match via the real
+/// `pgrep -x` (killall semantics), same exclusion set as [buildPkillShim].
+/// Any flag the shim does not model (`-i`, `-q`, `-u`, `-o`, `-y`, …)
+/// execs the real `killall`.
+String buildKillallShim({
+  required String realKillall,
+  required String realPgrep,
+}) =>
+    r'''#!/bin/sh
+# fa bash-guard shim for killall (gh-1763): never signals the harness or
+# its ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.
+set -u
+FA_REAL_KILLALL='__FA_REAL_KILLALL__'
+FA_REAL_PGREP='__FA_REAL_PGREP__'
+
+sig=''
+names=''
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --signal) sig="${2-}"; shift 2 ;;
+    --signal=*) sig="${1#--signal=}"; shift ;;
+    -[0-9]*) sig="$1"; shift ;;
+    -[Ss][Ii][Gg][A-Za-z]*|-[A-Z][A-Z]*) sig="$1"; shift ;;
+    -*) exec "$FA_REAL_KILLALL" "$@" ;;
+    *) names="$names $1"; shift ;;
+  esac
+done
+[ -n "$names" ] || exec "$FA_REAL_KILLALL" "$@"
+
+self=$$
+parent="${PPID:-}"
+out=0
+for n in $names; do
+  pids=$("$FA_REAL_PGREP" -x "$n" 2>/dev/null) || continue
+  for p in $pids; do
+    case " ${FA_PROTECTED_PIDS:-} " in *" $p "*) continue ;; esac
+    if [ "$p" = "$parent" ] || [ "$p" = "$self" ]; then continue; fi
+    if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
+      kill "$sig" "$p" 2>/dev/null && out=1
+    else
+      kill -TERM "$p" 2>/dev/null && out=1
+    fi
+  done
+done
+[ "$out" -eq 1 ] && exit 0
+exit 1
+'''
+        .replaceAll('__FA_REAL_KILLALL__', realKillall)
+        .replaceAll('__FA_REAL_PGREP__', realPgrep);
+
+/// The per-process bash guard: a private temp dir holding the PATH shims
+/// and the protected pid set injected into every bash tool call. [shimDir]
+/// is null when no shim applied (pkill/killall/pgrep missing on the host) —
+/// the pid set still arms the `kill()` prelude.
+///
+/// The shim dir is deliberately NOT deleted at process exit: a concurrent
+/// bash call in another fa process may be mid-lookup, and unlinking under
+/// it would turn `pkill` into an exec failure. Cost: one ~2 KB dir per fa
+/// process launch in `$TMPDIR` (OS tmp reapers bound it).
+final class BashGuardProvision {
+  /// Creates the provision. Never throws on the caller side: provisioning
+  /// failures degrade to a null provision instead.
+  const BashGuardProvision({
+    required this.shimDir,
+    required this.protectedPids,
+  });
+
+  /// Private temp dir (0700) with the executable `pkill`/`killall` shims;
+  /// prepended to PATH. Null when no shim applies.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

## PR Description

Closes #1763
# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity.
- Full default suite: `+11961 ~62`, **zero failures attributable to this change** — `dart analyze` clean, CRAP diff gate OK, `test/providers/` green in isolation.

### Notes
- All 17 suite failures attributed by controlled experiment: `test/browser_ext/` ×5 fail identically on the pre-fix tree (no DBus for Chrome; owns `browser-ext.yml`); 11 integration legs fail only when the dev agent's `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` env leaks into spawned sessions — **green with the `FA*` vars scrubbed**, incl. the new SIGTERM assertion; `composer_tui_grid_pty` ×1 is a pre-existing render flake (3/3 failures pre-fix).

+library;

+/// The env var carrying the protected pid set into every bash tool call

+const String bashGuardPidsEnv = 'FA_PROTECTED_PIDS';
+
+/// The env var carrying the shim dir path into every bash tool call (the
+/// PATH itself is prepended by `_environment`; the variable exists so the
+/// contract has one owner here).
+const String bashGuardShimDirEnv = 'FA_GUARD_SHIM_DIR';
+
+/// The guard prelude prepended to every bash tool script (POSIX):
+///
+/// - `set --` restores `sh -c` positional-parameter parity (`$#` = 0, empty
+///   `"$@"`) — the `. "$1"` delivery otherwise leaves the script path as
+///   `$1`.
+/// - `kill()` filters [bashGuardPidsEnv] pids (and their `-pgid` group
+///   targets) out of the arguments before invoking the real `kill`. No
+///   protected hit → the call is passed through byte-identical. Every
+///   construct is `set -e`/`set -u`-safe (if-chains, guarded expansions).
+String bashGuardPrelude() =>
+    '''
+# ── fa bash-guard (gh-1763): self-defense prelude ──────────────────────
+# Restore sh -c positional-parameter parity, then keep kill() from
+# signaling the harness/ancestor pids exported via $bashGuardPidsEnv.
+set --
+kill() {
+  __fa_rest=''
+  __fa_pids_left=0
+  __fa_hit=0
+  for __fa_a in "\$@"; do
+    case "\$__fa_a" in
+      ''|-|--|%*|-[A-Za-z]*)
+        __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+        ;;
+      -[0-9]*)
+        __fa_n="\${__fa_a#-}"
+        __fa_keep=1
+        for __fa_p in \${$bashGuardPidsEnv:-}; do
+          if [ "\$__fa_n" = "\$__fa_p" ]; then __fa_keep=0; break; fi
+        done
+        if [ "\$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
+          __fa_hit=1
+        else
+          __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+        fi
+        ;;
+      *)
+        __fa_keep=1
+        for __fa_p in \${$bashGuardPidsEnv:-}; do
+          if [ "\$__fa_a" = "\$__fa_p" ]; then __fa_keep=0; break; fi
+        done
+        if [ "\$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
+          __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+          __fa_pids_left=\$((__fa_pids_left + 1))
+        else
+          __fa_hit=1
+        fi
+        ;;
+    esac
+  done
+  if [ "\$__fa_hit" = 0 ]; then
+    command kill "\$@"
+    return
+  fi
+  __fa_rc=0
+  if [ "\$__fa_pids_left" -gt 0 ]; then

+    command kill \$__fa_rest || __fa_rc=\$?
+  fi
+  echo 'fa: kill skipped protected pid(s) (gh-1763 bash-guard)' >&2
+  return "\$__fa_rc"

+''';

+/// same selection engine and flags), filters the protected pids, the
+/// invoking shell (`PPID`) and the shim itself, then signals the rest with
+/// the requested signal (default `SIGTERM`). Selection shapes the shim

+/// `-o`, …) exec the real `pkill` — honest behavior over silent guessing.
+String buildPkillShim({required String realPkill, required String realPgrep}) =>
+    r'''#!/bin/sh
+# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
+# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.

+FA_REAL_PKILL='__FA_REAL_PKILL__'
+FA_REAL_PGREP='__FA_REAL_PGREP__'

+sel=''

+# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)

+    -[a-zA-Z]*)

+      fa_rest="$fa_body"
+      while [ -n "$fa_rest" ]; do
+        fa_c="${fa_rest%"${fa_rest#?}"}"
+        case "$fa_c" in

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

+# fa bash-guard shim for pkill (gh-1763): never signals the harness or its
+# ancestor chain, the invoking shell, or itself.

+FA_REAL_PGREP='__FA_REAL_PGREP__'

+sig=''
+sel=''

+# mode prints a number the loop would read as a pid, v = negated match)

+  case "$a" in
+    -[a-zA-Z]*)

+        [0-9]*|[Ss][Ii][Gg]*|[A-Z]*) continue ;;

+done

**A2 confirmed**: a PROTECTED group target (`kill -TERM -5902` with `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS=5902`) passed straight through to the real `kill` — the dummy was killed. This is the exact protection failure the prelude claims to prevent (dartdoc: "`kill()` filters [bashGuardPidsEnv] pids (and their `-pgid` group targets) out of the arguments"). The negative-pid branch's keep/hit logic is inverted relative to the positive-pid branch.

And the killer scenario: `kill -9 -$(pgid of harness)` — e.g. an LM-generated `kill -- -<pgid>` sweeping stale process groups — still kills the harness group. The root bug class (harness killed by child's own kill) survives via the `-PGID` spelling.

Also the mixed case: `kill -TERM -<protected_pgid> <unprotected_pid>` → hit=0 → full pass-through → protected group signaled too. And `kill -TERM -<unprotected> <unprotected pid>` → the group silently dropped while pid killed.

- **Author**: ai-teammate

## PR Description

Closes #1763
# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity.
- Full default suite: `+11961 ~62`, **zero failures attributable to this change** — `dart analyze` clean, CRAP diff gate OK, `test/providers/` green in isolation.

### Notes
- All 17 suite failures attributed by controlled experiment: `test/browser_ext/` ×5 fail identically on the pre-fix tree (no DBus for Chrome; owns `browser-ext.yml`); 11 integration legs fail only when the dev agent's `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` env leaks into spawned sessions — **green with the `FA*` vars scrubbed**, incl. the new SIGTERM assertion; `composer_tui_grid_pty` ×1 is a pre-existing render flake (3/3 failures pre-fix).

## PR Description

Closes #1763
# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity.
- Full default suite: `+11961 ~62`, **zero failures attributable to this change** — `dart analyze` clean, CRAP diff gate OK, `test/providers/` green in isolation.

### Notes
- All 17 suite failures attributed by controlled experiment: `test/browser_ext/` ×5 fail identically on the pre-fix tree (no DBus for Chrome; owns `browser-ext.yml`); 11 integration legs fail only when the dev agent's `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` env leaks into spawned sessions — **green with the `FA*` vars scrubbed**, incl. the new SIGTERM assertion; `composer_tui_grid_pty` ×1 is a pre-existing render flake (3/3 failures pre-fix).

    "summary": "gh-1763 [BUG] bash tool pkill -f self-matches its own sh -c wrapper (exit -15) and aborts the fa session with exit 130 (gh-1746 run 39661276610)",
    "description": "Closes #1763
# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity.
- Full default suite: `+11961 ~62`, **zero failures attributable to this change** — `dart analyze` clean, CRAP diff gate OK, `test/providers/` green in isolation.

### Notes
- All 17 suite failures attributed by controlled experiment: `test/browser_ext/` ×5 fail identically on the pre-fix tree (no DBus for Chrome; owns `browser-ext.yml`); 11 integration legs fail only when the dev agent's `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` env leaks into spawned sessions — **green with the `FA*` vars scrubbed**, incl. the new SIGTERM assertion; `composer_tui_grid_pty` ×1 is a pre-existing render flake (3/3 failures pre-fix)."
  }
}

+library;

+import 'dart:io';
+
+/// The env var carrying the protected pid set into every bash tool call
+/// (space-separated): the harness pid, its ancestor chain up to init, and
+/// the harness process group. The `kill()` prelude and both shims read it.
+const String bashGuardPidsEnv = 'FA_PROTECTED_PIDS';
+
+/// The env var carrying the shim dir path into every bash tool call (the
+/// PATH itself is prepended by `_environment`; the variable exists so the
+/// contract has one owner here).
+const String bashGuardShimDirEnv = 'FA_GUARD_SHIM_DIR';
+
+/// The guard prelude prepended to every bash tool script (POSIX):
+///
+/// - `set --` restores `sh -c` positional-parameter parity (`$#` = 0, empty
+///   `"$@"`) — the `. "$1"` delivery otherwise leaves the script path as
+///   `$1`.
+/// - `kill()` filters [bashGuardPidsEnv] pids (and their `-pgid` group
+///   targets) out of the arguments before invoking the real `kill`. No
+///   protected hit → the call is passed through byte-identical. Every
+///   construct is `set -e`/`set -u`-safe (if-chains, guarded expansions).
+String bashGuardPrelude() =>
+    '''
+# ── fa bash-guard (gh-1763): self-defense prelude ──────────────────────
+# Restore sh -c positional-parameter parity, then keep kill() from
+# signaling the harness/ancestor pids exported via $bashGuardPidsEnv.
+set --
+kill() {
+  __fa_rest=''
+  __fa_pids_left=0
+  __fa_hit=0
+  for __fa_a in "\$@"; do
+    case "\$__fa_a" in
+      ''|-|--|%*|-[A-Za-z]*)
+        __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+        ;;
+      -[0-9]*)
+        __fa_n="\${__fa_a#-}"
+        __fa_keep=1
+        for __fa_p in \${$bashGuardPidsEnv:-}; do
+          if [ "\$__fa_n" = "\$__fa_p" ]; then __fa_keep=0; break; fi
+        done
+        if [ "\$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then
+          __fa_hit=1
+        else
+          __fa_rest="\$__fa_rest \$__fa_a"
+        fi
+        ;;
+      *)
+        __fa_keep=1
+        for __fa_p in \${$bashGuardPidsEnv:-}; do
+          if [ "\$__fa_a" = "\$__fa_p" ]; then __fa_keep=0; break; fi
+        done
+        if [ "\$__fa_keep" = 1 ]; then

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1763` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +809
- **Deletions**: -32
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T22:14:35Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T00:21:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #1763
# gh-1763 — `pkill -f` self-matches the bash tool's own `sh -c` wrapper

### Root Cause
- Every POSIX bash call ran as `sh -c '<command>'`, so the whole script sat in the wrapper's own argv — any `pkill -f <pattern>` inside the command killed its own shell before the target (`sleep 30` survived, call died exit -15). The sweep could also catch the harness pid chain.

### Fix
- `lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart` (new): per-process guard — PATH shims for `pkill`/`killall` + a `kill()` prelude that skip the harness pid chain/process group (`FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`) and the invoking shell; real victims still match. Provision failure degrades to legacy behavior.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart`: POSIX scripts delivered from a per-exec temp file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>`, `$0`/`$#`-parity prelude) so wrapper argv never carries the body; guard dir + pid set merged into every exec env; headless `SIGTERM` aborts log `fa: SIGTERM received …` (130/143 contract unchanged). Windows keeps `cmd /c`.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, `bin/fah_util.dart`: same SIGTERM log on headless paths. `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: contract documented.

### Test Coverage
- `test/env/bash_self_defense_test.dart` (new, 13): `pkill -f <unique>; echo survived` exits 0 through `exec`, `startShellJob` and the `bash` tool (RED pre-fix: exit -15); `pgrep -f` no longer self-lists; protected-pid exemption for shim+`kill()` with a real dummy still reaped; script parity.
- Full default suite: `+11961 ~62`, **zero failures attributable to this change** — `dart analyze` clean, CRAP diff gate OK, `test/providers/` green in isolation.

### Notes
- All 17 suite failures attributed by controlled experiment: `test/browser_ext/` ×5 fail identically on the pre-fix tree (no DBus for Chrome; owns `browser-ext.yml`); 11 integration legs fail only when the dev agent's `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` env leaks into spawned sessions — **green with the `FA*` vars scrubbed**, incl. the new SIGTERM assertion; `composer_tui_grid_pty` ×1 is a pre-existing render flake (3/3 failures pre-fix).
